installer.ifa

Installer Architecture

How Ifá-Lang installation works across platforms.

Crates

Crate Purpose
ifa-installer-core Platform-independent installation logic
ifa-installer-gui Graphical installer UI (egui)

Core Modules

Source: crates/ifa-installer-core/src/

Module Purpose
install.rs Main installation flow with RAII transaction rollback
uninstall.rs Clean removal with safety checks
extraction.rs ZIP/tar.gz archive extraction with path traversal protection
net.rs Download from GitHub releases with SHA256 verification
check.rs System requirements check (RAM, disk, OS)
config.rs Installation configuration (directory, PATH, offline mode)
profiles.rs Component list (single ifa CLI binary)
args.rs CLI argument parsing via clap
windows.rs Windows PATH (registry), with rollback on failure
unix.rs Shell detection (zsh/bash/fish) and rc file updates

Installation Flow

1. Check system requirements (2GB RAM, 1GB disk)
2. Fetch release metadata from GitHub API
3. Download SHA256SUMS for verification
4. For each component:
   a. Check for local sidecar archive
   b. Verify checksum (if available)
   c. Extract (ZIP or tar.gz)
5. Platform setup:
   - Windows: Add to PATH via HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Environment
   - Unix: Append export to shell rc file
6. Commit transaction (RAII rollback on failure)

CLI Usage

# Interactive GUI (or headless with --headless)
ifa-installer

# Headless install with defaults
ifa-installer --headless

# Auto-accept prompts
ifa-installer --headless --yes

# Custom install directory
ifa-installer --headless --dir /opt/ifa

# Uninstall
ifa-installer --headless --uninstall

Rollback

The installer uses InstallTransaction (RAII) for automatic rollback on failure. All extracted files are tracked; if any step fails, they are deleted on drop. On success, the transaction is committed to prevent cleanup.

// RAII guard: files are tracked and cleaned up if not committed
struct InstallTransaction { ... }
impl Drop for InstallTransaction {
    // Removes all tracked files on rollback
}
